paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: rest isn't something you find by getting your life in order. It's something you find in a Person. David says, "In God alone my soul finds rest," and he says it while people are out to knock him down (Psalm 62:1, 3). His rest didn't wait for the trouble to quiet down. It sat on God, his rock, his salvation and his fortress (Psalm 62:2).

So where do YOU put your weight when things get shaky? David tells us what won't hold it. People are "but a vapor," riches can pile up, and he says, "do not set your heart upon them" (Psalm 62:9-10). That's like leaning on a cookie that's still warm from the oven, friend. Looks solid, then it's crumbs. David says to "pour out your hearts before Him," because "God is our refuge" (Psalm 62:8).

And here's the part that settles it. David says, "God has spoken once; I have heard this twice: that power belongs to God, and loving devotion to You, O Lord" (Psalm 62:11-12). The One with ALL the power is the same One full of loving devotion, so you can trust Him at all times and rest. And David ends by telling the Lord, "You will repay each man according to his deeds" (Psalm 62:12).
